blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: I bought a clothes rack from IKEA.
exercises.why: The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену. Я жду письма.* — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The accusative case is used to denote the direct object of the preceding verb and answers the questions кого? — whom? or что? — what?» — DLI, Lesson 18.
exercises.context: The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену.

exercises.why: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. — Я не пью молока. Я вижу реку. — Я не вижу реки.* The verb ждать takes no preposition. The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену. Я жду письма.* — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks, «Genitive case».
exercises.context: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. — Я не пью молока.
